newsitem.title: ITALY: Scalfaro praises Italian government on budget.
newsitem.headline: Scalfaro praises Italian government on budget.

text.p: Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro thanked the government on Saturday for approving a tough 1997 budget which could allow Italy to join the first wave of countries in a single European currency.

A statement from his office said Prime Minister Romano Prodi, Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco and Transport Minister Claudio Burlando met Scalfaro on Saturday and illustrated the 62.5 trillion budget package to him.

The statement said the president "expressed his heart-felt thanks to the prime minister and his cabinet for having tackled in a responsible and concrete way the complex problems of the state finances, in view of European deadlines".
The government approved the budget after an 11-hour meeting on Friday.

The package will cut a total of 62.5 trillion lire off next year's public sector deficit, aiming to reduce Italy's deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) ratio to three percent by the end of next year.
Achievement of the three percent deficit target would put Italy on course to join a group of countries establishing a single European currency in 1999.
